clue.text: Depressing sound of a story-telling brother

indicators.note: the clue asks for what a word sounds like when spoken, not how it is written

parts.note: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm were the brothers who collected fairy tales

explanation.surface: A gloomy noise is attributed to one of the famous fairy-tale brothers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound of' signals a homophone: GRIMM, the fairy-tale brothers' surname, is said the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bleak and dispiriting is depressing, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Footwear James tries to get rid of audibly

indicators.note: the pieces are to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.words: James tries to get rid of
parts.note: Jim is a short form of James, and the possessive gives JIM'S; to shoo is to drive away, so someone who tries to get rid of a pest shoos it

explanation.surface: A man called James wants to throw out some footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audibly' says that JIM'S plus SHOOS, spoken together, sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plimsolls worn for PE are a type of footwear.

clue.text: Traveller gets a bit wet crossing Dartmoor peak

indicators.note: the word for wet goes across and over the peak, holding it inside

parts.note: moist means slightly wet
a tor is a rocky hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A traveller gets damp walking over a hill on Dartmoor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts TOR inside MOIST. Dartmoor is a moorland in Devon famous for its granite tors.
explanation.definitionFit: A car driver is a road traveller.

clue.text: An old fellow with plenty of bottle

explanation.surface: Describes an elderly man with lots of nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' looks like British slang for courage, but here it is literal: a large wine bottle holding eight standard ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical patriarch lived 969 years, so his name means a very aged man; it also names a big champagne bottle.

clue.text: At the same time, it sounds like a nasty trick

indicators.note: the clue openly says the next words match the answer when spoken

parts.note: mean means nasty and a wile is a trick

explanation.surface: Meanwhile, the speaker hears something like a spiteful ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAN WILE, a nasty trick, is pronounced like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means during the intervening time, simultaneously.

clue.text: Man's offshore jet diverted for us president

indicators.note: the letters are turned aside from their order, so they get rearranged

parts.note: the possessive 's adds an S here as part of the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone's jet flying offshore is rerouted for the American president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diverted' rearranges MANSOFFSHOREJET into the president's name; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The third holder of the office and author of the Declaration of Independence was a US president.

clue.text: Sort of problem requiring group support

parts.note: a set is a group of things
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A problem arises that needs a team behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse or hitch is a kind of problem that sets progress back.

clue.text: Natural inclinations to be single man, somehow avoiding maiden

indicators.note: says the remaining letters get arranged in some other way
the letter for maiden is left out of the words

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A bachelor has natural tendencies to steer clear of young women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops M (maiden) from SINGLE MAN to leave SINGLEAN; 'somehow' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendencies or preferences one has are inclinations.

clue.text: Location in Middlesex has to grab you

indicators.note: one word seizes the other and holds it inside

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A place in Middlesex has to seize you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to grab' puts YE inside HAS. Hayes is a town in west London, historically in the county of Middlesex.
explanation.definitionFit: The named town is a place in the old county of Middlesex.

clue.text: Sacred text produced by fellow with paintings around

parts.note: a fellow is a man

indicators.note: the word for paintings is turned round to read the other way

parts.note: paintings collectively are art

explanation.surface: A holy text is written by a man surrounded by pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns ART into TRA, placed after MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A chant or formula repeated in Hindu or Buddhist practice is a sacred text.

clue.text: Someone late being reported

parts.note: late here means dead, not tardy: a newspaper account of a person who has died

explanation.definitionFit: A notice in the press covering a person recently deceased reports on the late individual.

clue.text: School's distress

explanation.surface: A school is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a well-known English public school; as a verb, harrow means to distress or torment.

clue.text: A very good set of stars — there's a lot of buzz about them

definitions.text: there's a lot of buzz about them

parts.note: pi is crossword shorthand for pious, very good
Aries is a constellation, the Ram

explanation.surface: An excellent constellation causes great excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buzz' looks like hype but means the humming of bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Places where bees are kept hum with buzzing insects.

clue.text: Fish container needed by sailor

parts.note: a skip is a large container for builders' rubbish
Jack, as in Jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor needs a box to hold the fish.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the British term for a large open waste container.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuna variety, the bonito, is a fish.

clue.text: Item of furniture on which diamonds may be displayed

definitions.text: Item of furniture on which diamonds may be displayed

parts.words: Item of furniture on which diamonds may be displayed
parts.note: diamonds are the playing-card suit, not jewels, laid out on a table during a game

explanation.definitionFit: Small folding tables for bridge or whist are where hands of playing cards are laid down.

clue.text: Strip brings endless reprimand

indicators.note: the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to slate is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: A stripping off results in a never-ending scolding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the last letter from SLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin flat strip of wood or metal, as in a blind.

clue.text: Trusted friend could make Leo great

indicators.note: the letters could be remade into a new word

explanation.surface: A close companion could turn Leo into a great man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges LEOGREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A second self, or an intimate companion, is a trusted friend.

clue.text: A little girl unaltered

parts.note: sis is short for sister, a girl

explanation.surface: A small girl has not changed.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in the existing state, without changes.

clue.text: The man in new estate is an arty type

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the rearranged letters
makes the word into something new, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man in a new housing estate is artistic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges ESTATE to AESTTE, and 'in' puts HE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone devoted to beauty and art is an arty type.

clue.text: Enjoyed being rescued outside old Abraham's place

indicators.note: the word for rescued sits around the other pieces

parts.note: saved means rescued
Ur of the Chaldees was Abraham's birthplace in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone relished being saved near Abraham's ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts O plus UR inside SAVED.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish food or an experience is to enjoy it.

clue.text: Prince and queen favouring church of England inevitably

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for queen
to be for something is to favour it

explanation.surface: Royalty supporting the established church is unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means by necessity, unavoidably.

clue.text: A street flanked by clean grass

indicators.note: the word for clean stands on either side of the other pieces

parts.note: pure means clean

explanation.surface: A road lined on both sides by clean grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flanked by' puts A ST inside PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grazing land covered with grass is pasture.

clue.text: Fortress has alcoholic drink — something treasured

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A castle stocks booze, a prized possession.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento kept for sentimental reasons is treasured.

clue.text: What wilkinson does thrills!

explanation.surface: A sportsman's action gives excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonny Wilkinson was England's famous rugby goal-kicker.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby star made his name by booting the ball; slang for excitement or buzz is also the same word.

clue.text: Design tawdry items with ducks on

parts.note: tat is cheap and shoddy goods
to can mean on, as in a door pushed to
a duck is a score of nothing, O, in cricket

explanation.surface: Tacky goods are decorated with ducks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducks' is plural but gives only one O; the setter's intent may be TO plus O, with 'with' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern inked into the skin is a design.

clue.text: Draughts in PM's country house

explanation.surface: A board game at the prime minister's retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers; Chequers is the British prime minister's official country residence.
explanation.definitionFit: An old name for the board game of checkers; also the country home of the British prime minister.

clue.text: One supplying drink in little brown jug

parts.note: BR is a short form, a little version, of brown
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: Someone serving drink keeps it in a small brown pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer maker supplies drink.

clue.text: Lost, one hen gets to traverse this ancient site

indicators.note: the answer runs across the words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A missing chicken has to cross an old monument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to traverse' signals a run of letters spanning 'Lost, one hen gets'.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric stone circle in Wiltshire is an ancient site.

clue.text: Aim to restrict independent woman

indicators.note: one word confines the other inside it

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A goal limits a woman's independence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrict' puts I inside END.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, so it stands for any woman.
